item.title: Mike Johnson, “isn’t this your job?”
item.description: Speaker Mike Johnson lashed out at a reporter, calling him “stupid” for asking about Johnson’s culpability in the Iran War. Jessica Tarlov and Aaron Parnas discuss, on Raging Perspective.
item.content:encoded:
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PHNHabxOjKM

Transcript

On Iran, you said repeatedly that this war was going to be over soon. You said that this would be a temporary blip on short term on gas prices. It is still more than six months. People are getting hurt still at the pump. Should the American people not also judge you on your projections here that were clearly off base? >> I don't know who that is. It's one of the stupidest questions you've ever asked. >> Why is that so stupid? >> I have nothing to do with the prosecution of the war across the globe. >> Uh-oh. >> But they're so rude. >> That's not Southern hospitality. >> The idea that the speaker of the house shouldn't be held responsible for any of

the comments that he makes, which are supposed to be rooted in things like briefings and relationships with the people in the administration up to the president, who he definitely has on speed dial, is ludicrous. >> Isn't it in Congress's job to approve a war? >> We're forgetting that that is what Congress's job is is to have oversight over war.

item.title: AOC “probably” wouldn’t date a republican
item.description: Newly single Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) was asked if she would ever date someone across the political aisle. Jessica Tarlov and Aaron Parnas discuss, on Raging Perspective.
item.content:encoded:
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/TLcVxY6i3r4

Transcript

Would you ever date a conservative? In any Is that anything you'd ever entertain? >> Um, I have to say it's uh probably not. >> [laughter] >> Don't date across the aisle? >> No, you know, but I think a lot of politics sometimes, at least for me, is about values and being aligned with um in values, I think, is tremendously important. >> Hot girl single summer. But she's making an important point, which is borne out

by the data on this. People now do not want to have relationships or get involved with folks across ideological lines. >> I will say when my wife and I first started dating, I was conservative and she was Bernie bro liberal. And um we would not have lasted if we remained on those ideological playing fields. >> Yeah, my husband, who is probably to the left of me in general, um loves to troll me about Bernie Sanders, cuz I love Hillary so much. He'll just be like, Bernie would have won. And then

I lose it.

item.title: "Canadian consumers have something Americans don't."
item.description: Trump’s attempt to intimidate Canada and Prime Minister Mark Carney are destined to backfire — even if Canada might suffer in the short-term. It’s a betrayal of what’s made America work over the past 80 years, according to Scott Galloway and Jessica Tarlov on Raging Moderates.
item.content:encoded:
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/K5vVXbacJxQ

Transcript

Canada's new counter tariffs are officially in effect despite escalating threats from Trump in recent days. He even floated the idea that he might end all trade with Canada. He also posted an image of him and Prime Minister Mark Carney as hockey players with Carney on the ice and Trump shouting, "Get up, Governor." >> 93, "Get up, Governor." Like, you kind of can't hate this guy enough. >> Yeah, look, one of them is a leader who acquits himself with dignity and grace and is befitting of his position. The other is Donald Trump. This is like a divorce where you live in the same town, go to the same church, and live in the same house. Like all tariffs, the person

who initiated it likely ends up on the losing end of this because Canadian consumers have something American consumers don't have and that is resolved. Canadians are rallied behind this. They are really upset and angry. They're going after the heart and lungs of some of these red states. >> I'm overwhelmed by the precision with which Canada is doing this and the slop factory that seems to be our trade apparatus at this point. We have no reporting that there has been anything

close to another round of negotiations or a deal. >> We don't cooperate with our allies. We're under the impression that we're the only part that matters and not recognizing the last 80 years our strength has come from a whole that's greater than the sum of its parts in terms of our alliances and democracies and being seen as the good guys. And to be clear, Canada has not grown their economy in 10 years. It is not a well-run economy. But the reason why they will ultimately win this trading war despite registering more pain is because they have the support of the

Canadian people.
